findings.title: canManage() grants manage access to admins holding only the 'view' scope on Groups
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the fallback checks hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), i.e. the VIEW scope alone satisfies canManage(). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() guards group creation with auth.groups().requireManage(), so any admin who has been granted only the 'view' scope on the all-groups resource (or who matches a view permission) can create new top-level groups in the realm. canManage() should only check the MANAGE scope (compare canView() on line 52, which correctly checks VIEW and MANAGE).

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() mixes up authorization Resource IDs with group IDs
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the callback passes groupResource.getId() (the authorization store Resource ID) into hasPermission(), which does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) — but per-group resources are named by the group ID (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup/getOrCreateResource), so findByName with the Resource ID finds nothing and silently falls back to the all-groups resource evaluation. Worse, granted.add(groupResource.getId()) adds the Resource store ID, not the group ID. Callers (UsersResource.searchForUser, BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser, UsersResource.getUsersCount) put this set into the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute / count queries to filter users by group membership, so the filter uses non-existent group IDs and a fine-grained admin with view-members/manage-members permission on a group will see zero users instead of that group's members.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the all-groups resource does not exist
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(), when no per-group resource is found, resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) can return null (getResourceTypeResource returns null when the resource type resource is not found in the store, e.g. the admin-permissions client schema was not initialized for this resource server). The next line calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) without a null check, causing a NullPointerException instead of cleanly denying access. UserPermissionsV2 has the same pattern, but there the 'Users' resource is guaranteed by V1 initialization; for the newly added Groups type the all-groups resource may not exist on older realms that enabled admin permissions before this schema change.
